mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by at least 0.25% in three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a financial crisis with inverted yield curve.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or during periods of unusually strong productivity growth.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening consumer demand, which reduces revenue growth for consumer-facing firms and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or during periods of offsetting fiscal stimulus.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or during periods of strong export demand.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (CPI) above their 12-month averages signals a monetary tightening accompanied by rising inflation, increasing real interest rates and eroding real corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both above 12-month averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or during periods of strong global demand offsetting domestic headwinds.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 1% month-over-month, sustained for two consecutive months, signals a rapid labor market expansion that can outpace productivity, raising wage pressures and reducing profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month + 1% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or during periods of unusually high productivity growth.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) below their 12-month averages in the same month signals a broad-based weakening in demand, which reduces corporate revenues and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both below 12-month averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or during periods of strong fiscal stimulus.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals a manufacturing expansion, which boosts earnings for industrial firms and predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or during periods of supply chain disruptions despite rising output.
